newsitem.title: UK: Minet decision due in weeks - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Minet decision due in weeks - analysts.

text.p: A decision on the future of insurance broker Minet is expected within weeks following confirmation from owner St Pauls Cos that it is in talks with Marsh & McLennan Cos Inc.
"They must be quite well down the line on due diligence. I would think we'll hear within three to four weeks," said one London based insurance analyst.
Other analysts said that after yesterday's holding announcement, a decision on whether or not the deal would go ahead was likely within two to six weeks
St Pauls brought in Goldman Sachs last August to assist in examining strategic alternatives for the London based international insurance broker.
In a statement yesterday, it said the sale would exclude Swett & Crawford Group and Minet Burn Roche.
London based analysts said they did not follow St Pauls closely and therefore could not forecast the likely sale price for Minet.
However, they noted that in recent deals, some insurance brokers had changed hands at one times annual brokerage or less, adding that Minet has made losses in recent years.
Minet, which was ranked ninth biggest broker in the world in one survey last year, had annual revenue of around $370 million in the year to end September 1995.
The company's strengths include professional indemnity business and contracts with the world's top six accountants.

The insurance broking sector suffers from global over capacity and has seen a number of mergers recently, including Lowndes Lambert with Fenchurch, JIB Group with Lloyd Thompson and Aon Corp's acquisition of Alexander & Alexander Services Inc.
With no sign of an end to the current soft market for insurance rates, the outlook for brokers remains difficult with further consolidation likely.
Morgan Stanley said in a recent note that it expected the shares of the two leading UK brokers, Willis Corroon Group Plc and Sedgwick Group Plc, to underperform.
